title: 1987 AHSME Problem 25
statement: \(ABC\) is a triangle: \(A=(0,0),\) \(B=(36,15),\) and both the coordinates of \(C\) are integers. What is the minimum area \(\triangle ABC\) can have?

solutions.text:
For \(C=(u,v),\) the area is \[ \frac12|36v-15u|. \] Since \(\gcd(36,15)=3,\) the smallest possible positive value of the determinant is at least \(3.\) It is attained, for example, by \(u=7,\ v=3,\) since \(36(3)-15(7)=3.\) Therefore the minimum area is \(\frac{3}{2}.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Write \(C=(u,v)\) and use the determinant formula for triangle area
Find the smallest positive value of \(|36v-15u|\) using \(\gcd(36,15)\)
